bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding your neuroscientist salary from hourly to annual

Whether you are a graduate neuroscientist or an experienced professional, converting your hourly rate to an annual salary helps you compare job offers and plan your finances. This guide uses the latest Fair Work award rates, tax tables, and superannuation rules to give you a clear picture of your **neuroscientist salary**.

### How the conversion works

The standard formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For full‑time employees under most modern awards, ordinary hours are 38 per week. If you work part‑time or casual, use your agreed weekly hours. The result is your gross annual income before tax and the Medicare levy.

For example, a neuroscientist at Level 1 (4‑year degree) under the Professional Employees Award 2020 earns a minimum hourly rate of $34.57. Multiplying by 38 hours and 52 weeks gives **$68,538 per year**.

### Award rates vs the National Minimum Wage

The National Minimum Wage, set by the Fair Work Commission, is $26.44 per hour from 1 July 2026. This applies only to employees not covered by an award or agreement. Most neuroscientists, however, are covered by the Professional Employees Award, which sets higher minimums. The award’s classification structure includes:

- Level 1 Graduate (3‑year degree): $33.71/hr → $66,825/yr
- Level 1 Graduate (4‑ or 5‑year degree): $34.57/hr → $68,538/yr
- Level 2 Experienced professional: $39.77/hr → $78,836/yr
- Level 3 Senior professional: $43.46/hr → $86,157/yr

These rates are the minimum; employers may pay above them. Always check your classification in the award or use the [pay guides](/blog) for your industry.

### Casual loading and part‑time work

If you work as a casual neuroscientist, you receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For the Level 1 (4‑year degree) rate, that becomes $43.21 per hour. The loading is paid instead of entitlements like annual leave and sick leave. Use our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page to see how it affects your take‑home pay.

Part‑time employees are paid the same hourly rate as full‑time employees but work fewer hours. Their annual salary is calculated pro‑rata: hourly rate × actual weekly hours × 52.

### Fortnightly and weekly pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To estimate your fortnightly gross pay, multiply your weekly pay by two. For a full‑time neuroscientist at $34.57/hr:

- Weekly: $34.57 × 38 = $1,313.66
- Fortnightly: $1,313.66 × 2 = $2,627.32

Your pay slip will show these amounts before tax and other deductions.

### Tax and the Medicare levy on your annual salary

Once you have your gross annual figure, the Australian Taxation Office applies the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15¢ for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30¢ for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37¢ for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001 and over: $51,370 plus 45¢ for each $1 over $190,000

In addition, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. For a neuroscientist earning $68,538, the tax would be approximately:

- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201–$45,000 (26,800): 15% = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001–$68,538 (23,538): 30% = $7,061.40
- Total tax: $11,081.40
- Medicare levy (2%): $1,370.76
- Total tax and Medicare: $12,452.16

Your take‑home pay would be roughly $56,086 per year. Use our [take‑home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a personalised estimate.

### Superannuation is paid on top

Employers must contribute superannuation at 12% of your ordinary earnings, on top of your salary. This is not deducted from your pay. For a $68,538 salary, that’s an extra $8,224.56 per year into your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more.

### Important notes

This conversion assumes you work the same hours every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It does not include salary sacrifice or the Medicare levy surcharge. Always check your specific award or agreement for exact entitlements.

For a quick estimate, use our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool. Enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading) and select your employment type to see annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures including tax and super.
